topic: Tarrare, the 18th-century French soldier whose insatiable appetite made him a document-swallowing military courier, and the fork he believed killed him
title: The French Spy Who Smuggled Secrets By Swallowing Them
description: AI-narrated commentary on the true story of Tarrare, the 18th-century French soldier whose bottomless appetite turned him into a document-smuggling military courier -- and later, a medical mystery that stumped his own doctors.

hook_candidates.text: This French soldier's stomach smuggled secret documents past enemy lines.
Would you trust top-secret war orders to a soldier who once ate live cats for breakfast?
Everyone assumes a swallowed fork killed this French soldier. His autopsy proved it wasn't the fork.
A starving French soldier's bottomless appetite turned him into his own army's strangest secret weapon.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who brags about their competitive eating record because they want to prove real history already beat them.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume a soldier's secret documents got smuggled using disguises, not swallowed inside his own stomach.
closing_comment: He really smuggled secrets by swallowing them, then spent his last years fighting a mystery illness doctors still debate today.

sources.note: Confirms his 1798 death at 26, his role as a document-smuggling military courier, and his tuberculosis autopsy.
Confirms the autopsy found no swallowed fork; his actual cause of death was tuberculosis, not the fork.
